scenario.draft:
Goal: Verify that the admin shipment search endpoint returns a correct, consistent paginated list of shipments with tracking fields derived from the latest non-deleted shipment confirmation.

Scenario 1 (primary success): Admin searches shipments by order and shipment status and receives correct tracking mapping
1) Create admin authorization by joining admin account.
2) Using the admin shipment search, submit a request with filters that narrow results to a known parent order id (shopping_mall_order_id) and optionally a specific shipment status (status), with page=1 and a reasonable limit (e.g., 10). Include a sort value that should deterministically order results (e.g., by created_at or status if supported by the service contract).
3) Validate response shape: it returns IPageIShoppingMallShipment.ISummary with pagination object (current, limit, records, pages) and data as an array.
4) For each shipment item in data:
   - Assert immutable mapping: id, status, sellerSnapshotId are present.
   - Assert order mapping: order object exists and includes order.id and order.orderCode.
   - Assert tracking consistency: trackingUrl, trackingNumber, carrierName, confirmationType, confirmedAt are either all null (when no non-deleted confirmation exists) OR correspond to exactly the latest non-deleted confirmation record for that shipment.
   - If multiple confirmations exist historically, validate that the returned tracking fields match the confirmation with the greatest confirmedAt (and tie-breaker by createdAt / newest confirmation record).
5) Edge within this scenario: Ensure that at least one returned shipment has non-null tracking fields and at least one has null tracking fields (prepare data accordingly in the test setup by selecting an order with both unconfirmed and confirmed shipments).

Scenario 2 (edge case): Admin search when shipments exist but some have only deleted confirmations
1) Create admin authorization.
2) Call shipment search with filters that return shipments that have confirmation rows where the latest confirmation is soft-deleted (deleted_at not null), but an earlier confirmation exists (also potentially deleted/non-deleted depending on test data).
3) Validate that tracking fields returned are derived only from the latest non-deleted confirmation. If all confirmations for a shipment are deleted, expect tracking fields to be null.
4) Validate that shipment status field still reflects shopping_mall_shipments.status, independent of confirmation deletion.

Scenario 3 (edge/pagination): Pagination returns correct boundaries and stable sorting
1) Create admin authorization.
2) Call shipment search with page=1, limit=2 and a deterministic sort.
3) Call shipment search again with page=2, limit=2 and the same filters/sort.
4) Validate:
   - data[0..1] on page 1 are different from page 2 entries (no overlap) when total records >= 3.
   - pagination.records and pagination.pages are consistent with limit.
   - The set of shipment ids across pages 1..N (where N=min(pages,2)) should preserve the deterministic order implied by the sort.

General validations for all scenarios:
- Response is not an error when no shipments match; it returns an empty data array with pagination reflecting records=0 (include this check if the test setup can create a filter that yields no results, but avoid exercising invalid filter input).

scenario.draft:
시나리오 1 (성공/정합성): 관리자가 한 번에 shipment 상태 및 seller shipment confirmation(추적 포함)을 업데이트할 때, 응답의 shipment.tracking 정보가 요청한 confirmation/추적 정보와 정확히 일치하는지 검증한다.

- 준비(인증): POST /shoppingMall/auth/admin/login 으로 admin 인증 컨텍스트를 확보한다.
- 준비(데이터): POST /shoppingMall/auth/member/join 으로 member 계정을 생성한 뒤, POST /shoppingMall/member/shipments 로 기존 order 기반 shipmentId를 확보한다. (해당 shipmentId는 PUT으로 수정 가능한 상태여야 한다.)
- 대상 호출: PUT /shoppingMall/admin/admin/shipments/{shipmentId}
  - 요청 바디에 shipment.status 를 변경하고, confirmation 관련 필드(confirmation_type, confirmed_at, tracking_url, tracking_number, carrier_name, note)를 함께 제공한다.
- 검증:
  1) 응답의 shipment.status 가 요청한 값으로 변경되었는지 확인한다.
  2) 응답의 shipment.tracking 이 null 이 아니어야 하며, tracking.confirmationType/confirmedAt 및 trackingUrl/trackingNumber/carrierName/note 가 입력과 일치하는지 확인한다.
  3) 동일 shipmentId에 대해 PUT을 한 번 더 호출해 status 는 변경하지 않고 추적 필드만 일부(예: tracking_number) 갱신한다. 이때 confirmationType/confirmedAt 는 유지되고 tracking 필드만 갱신되는지 확인한다.

핵심: shipment 상태/confirmation/tracking이 원자적으로 일관되게 업데이트되고, 의도치 않게 누락 필드가 덮어쓰지 않는지 검증한다.

   - Response conforms to IPageIShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ISummary: pagination has current, limit, records, pages; data is an array.

   - If multiple rows are returned, verify that ordering matches created_at desc based on the created_at values present in the returned items.

Pass criteria:
- 200 success.
- Pagination metadata is consistent (pages equals ceil(records/limit), data length <= limit).
- Deterministic ordering for the chosen sortBy/sortDirection and filtering (by created_at desc on returned items).

scenario.draft:
Test admin cancellation-request filtering using requested_at and seller_decisioned_at timeline windows, and verify includeDeleted and pagination behavior.

Steps:
1) Call POST /shoppingMall/auth/admin/join to create an authenticated admin session.
2) Call PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/admin/cancellation-requests with pagination (page=1, limit=20), includeDeleted=false, and sortBy=requested_at (descending). Do not set requestedAtFrom/requestedAtTo (or the equivalent request parameters for the requested_at window), and do not set an explicit seller_decisioned_at window; this is only to discover existing timeline values.
3) Select one returned record r0 and read its timeline value for requested_at (from the response field used by the API).
4) Define a narrow window around r0.requested_at using the same timestamp format/precision expected by the API (e.g., same timestamp bucket). Set requestedAtFrom and requestedAtTo (or the equivalent request parameters) to that narrow window while keeping includeDeleted=false and the same sortBy/sortDirection.
5) Call PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/admin/cancellation-requests again with page=1, limit=5, includeDeleted=false, and the narrow requested_at window.
6) Validate:
   - Every returned row’s requested_at value falls within [requestedAtFrom, requestedAtTo] (using the actual field name/format returned by the API).
   - Pagination is respected: returned data length is <= limit, and any pagination metadata (e.g., total/records) is consistent with the response.
7) Call PATCH a third time with the same pagination, sort, and requested_at window, but with includeDeleted=true.
8) Validate includeDeleted behavior without relying on strict monotonic page-size:
   - If the response includes total count/records metadata, assert includeDeleted=true has total >= includeDeleted=false for the same filters.
   - If only page data is available, assert that non-deleted records from the includeDeleted=false result are a subset of the includeDeleted=true result when matched by record identifiers.
   - For any row whose deleted_at is present and non-null, assert it is not null (deleted rows must expose deleted_at).

Pass criteria:
- Timeline window filters constrain the returned rows to the requested_at range.
- includeDeleted expands the result set (by total/records or by inclusion of non-deleted items), without requiring page-length monotonicity.
- Pagination bounds are respected (limit/page behavior consistent).

Test deleting an existing customer cancellation request as an administrator, and verify referential integrity and audit immutability.

Steps:
1) Register and authenticate an admin via the admin join endpoint; capture authorization tokens for subsequent admin calls.
2) Locate or create a scenario state where a cancellation request exists for a specific order item (use admin oversight listing if available in the test harness, or create required commerce records through existing flows). 3) Call DELETE /shoppingMall/admin/admin/cancellation-requests/{cancellationRequestId}.

Validations (success path):
- Response status indicates successful deletion (expected 204/empty body).
- The cancellation request record is no longer retrievable by its id in later reads (use the test harness to re-check via GET if available, otherwise verify via list/search that it is absent).
- The linked order item remains unchanged: its core fields and fulfillment/shipment/payment-relevant status must remain exactly as they were before the deletion.
- Any dispute-resolution snapshot records associated with this cancellation request remain available and unmodified (snapshot immutability): verify at least one corresponding snapshot is still retrievable and its payload/metadata is unchanged.

Edge checks within the same scenario:
- Confirm deletion is atomic: if the deletion fails, none of the linked entities (order item, shipment/payment, snapshots) should have changed.

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator can approve a refund request and that it updates exactly the targeted order item (and not other items), applies the refunded outcome consistently, and keeps shipment tracking and snapshot history coherent.

Steps/validations:
1) Admin joins to obtain admin access.
2) Member joins to obtain a member account.
3) Member creates a valid order item and then creates a refund request for that order item (initially in a pending/undecided workflow state).
4) Call PUT /shoppingMall/admin/admin/refund-requests/{refundRequestId} with an admin decision payload that sets the refund request to the approved/refunded decision outcome and includes an optional seller_comment.
5) Verify the response reflects the updated refund request: workflow outcome changed to the approved/refunded state; sellerComment is persisted; decisionedAt is non-null when moving out of pending; customerReason remains unchanged.
6) Verify isolation: locate the related order item linked by refundRequest.shopping_mall_order_item_id and confirm only that specific order item transitions to the refunded terminal state; other order items in the same order remain unchanged.
7) Shipment consistency: if the targeted order item is already linked to a shipment, validate that shipment-linked fulfillment/tracking state remains consistent with the refunded outcome (no contradictory tracking state).
8) Snapshot integrity: validate that an immutable snapshot record exists for the final decision transition and that prior history is not retroactively modified. If the system exposes snapshot linkage (e.g., via returned snapshot references or lookup-by-id behavior), ensure the snapshot is associated with the refund decision transition using the correct source identifiers.
9) Idempotency: re-submit the same admin decision update for the same refundRequestId and confirm the system does not create conflicting duplicate terminal-side effects or inconsistent duplicate final snapshots.

Failure/edge aspects to include (without testing HTTP 400 input validation):
- If the refund request is already terminally decided, verify the system either rejects the transition as a business conflict or returns the already-decided state without duplicating side effects, based on the API’s defined behavior.
- If a rejected/alternative decision path exists, verify decisionedAt handling and that the linked order item does not move to the refunded terminal state under the rejected outcome.

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator can reject a pending refund request and that it does NOT move the related order item into a refunded terminal state, while still preserving refund-request snapshot trail semantics.

6) Ensure isolation: other order items (same order) are unchanged.
7) Snapshot integrity: verify the system created a new immutable snapshot capturing the state transition for the refund request decision (including the reason). Confirm snapshot records are not retroactively modified.

Failure/edge aspects:
- If the refund request had already reached an approved/rejected terminal outcome, a second decision attempt must be rejected or treated as already-decided without applying conflicting order-item outcomes (business conflict prevention).

scenario.draft:
Test idempotency and conflict prevention when an administrator updates refund request decision multiple times, ensuring the system does not create conflicting repeated refund outcomes for the same order item and does not double-restore inventory.

Steps/validations:
1) Admin joins to obtain admin access.
2) Member creates an order item and then creates a refund request for it.
3) Admin calls PUT /shoppingMall/admin/admin/refund-requests/{refundRequestId} to approve/refund.
4) Capture resulting refund request status and the related order item line_item_status.
5) Re-issue the same PUT request with the same approved/refunded status and same seller_comment (or the exact same decision payload semantics).
6) Verify: (a) refund request remains in the same terminal approved status, (b) order item line_item_status remains refunded without additional changes, (c) inventory is not restored twice (use inventory history/audit if exposed via related endpoints; otherwise validate no duplicate inventory reconciliation signals), and (d) snapshot trail does not create multiple conflicting final snapshots for the same decision outcome.
7) Then attempt a conflicting decision transition (e.g., reject after approve) and validate the system rejects the conflicting transition or keeps state consistent per business conflict rules.

Business rule coverage:
- Prevent conflicting repeated refund outcomes per order item.
- Snapshot trail integrity remains consistent across retries and conflicting attempts.

Test Scenario B: Address ownership protection rejects cross-account update

- Validate: the response returns an address whose fields match the updated payload.
- Validate: the returned address ID remains the same.
- Validate: updatedAt changes (or at least the address shows the new updated timestamp) while deletedAt stays null.
- Validate: no address snapshot history is created/modified as a side effect (e.g., subsequent snapshot listing for that address should not show a new snapshot entry attributable to this update).

Scenario 2: Switching default address enforces exactly one active default per customer.
- Precondition: create a member account.

scenario.draft:
Scenario A: Member sees only their successfully-created orders, newest-first, with correct totals and derived overall status.

Steps:
1) Register a new member via POST /shoppingMall/auth/member/join and keep the returned authorization context for subsequent calls.
2) Using the authenticated member, create at least two distinct orders for the same member via POST /shoppingMall/member/orders:
   - Create one order that results in a successful order/placement outcome (so it is eligible to appear in order history).
   - Create one order with a non-successful placement outcome (e.g., failed payment attempt) such that it must be excluded by the order-history “successfully created” filter.
   Ensure order identifiers/order codes are distinct.
3) Call PATCH /shoppingMall/member/orders/history with an IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest that requests page=1 and a limit large enough to include both eligible orders.
   - If the request DTO supports sorting controls, set sorting to order-date semantics and sortDirection=desc; otherwise rely on the endpoint’s default newest-first behavior.
4) Validate response:
   - Response type is IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary and includes pagination metadata.
   - data contains only orders whose related payment status indicates success; the failed/non-success order must not appear.
   - ordering is newest-first by placedAt (shopping_mall_orders.placed_at desc). Verify that the first returned summary has the greatest placedAt among included orders.
   - For each returned order summary:
     * id and orderCode match the created eligible orders.
     * placedAt equals the placed_at timestamp stored on the corresponding created order.
     * totalPrice equals the SUM(order_items.seller_price_at_purchase * quantity) for that order, using the purchase-time values.
     * overallStatus is derived from the order item workflow (and shipment status where applicable) and matches the expected derived outcome for that order.
5) Confirm pagination: records equals the total count of eligible (successful) orders for this member, and returned data length is <= limit.

Key business checks:
- Data isolation: ensure no orders from any other member appear.
- Success filter: only successfully created/eligible-payment orders appear.
- Derived fields: totalPrice and overallStatus are consistent with stored purchase-time snapshots/workflow state.

scenario.draft:
Admin retrieves snapshot-history indices deterministically and respects authorization boundaries.

Scenario 1: Admin retrieves snapshot-history indices in deterministic order.
1) Authenticate as an administrator.
2) Use a reviewId that already has multiple snapshot-history index rows (e.g., from seeded test fixtures). Ensure the history includes both non-deleted and deleted history entries.

- Response conforms to IPageIShoppingMallReviewSnapshotsIndex.ISummary (pagination + data fields).

- Returned items are ordered by snapshotSequence ascending.
- For entries that represent deletion history, deletedAt is non-null; for non-deleted history entries, deletedAt is null.

Scenario 2: Admin retrieves an empty snapshot-history when no index entries exist.
1) Authenticate as an administrator.
2) Use a reviewId that exists in seeded fixtures but has zero snapshot-history index rows.
3) Call GET /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/snapshot-indices.

Validations:
- Response returns an empty data array.
- Pagination indicates empty results (e.g., total/records count is 0 and page metadata is consistent with the pagination contract).
- No errors.

Scenario 3: Authorization boundary for non-admin callers.
1) Authenticate as an administrator (to obtain a known reviewId from seeded fixtures).
2) Authenticate as a different authenticated member that is neither admin nor the review owner.
3) Call GET /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/snapshot-indices with the member credentials.

Validations:
- The request is rejected due to authorization.
- Do not leak sensitive existence details: failure behavior should be consistent with an authorization/non-privileged access response (without exposing whether the reviewId exists).

scenario.draft:
Scenario: Lock an owned address for checkout creates an immutable snapshot and preserves shipping details consistency

Steps:
1) Authenticate as a member by calling POST /shoppingMall/auth/member/join.
2) Create a saved shipping address owned by this member via POST /shoppingMall/member/addresses. Capture the returned address.id.
3) Call POST /shoppingMall/member/addresses/{addressId}/lock-for-checkout using the captured address.id.
4) Immediately call GET /shoppingMall/member/addresses/{addressId}/snapshots to obtain the address snapshot list created for checkout locking. Select the newest snapshot.
5) Record the newest snapshot’s recipient and destination/shipping fields from the response.
6) Call POST /shoppingMall/member/addresses/{addressId}/lock-for-checkout again with the same addressId.
7) Re-call GET /shoppingMall/member/addresses/{addressId}/snapshots and verify either:
   - the newest snapshot is reused (no conflicting newer snapshot data), or
   - a new snapshot is created but the stored snapshot fields still reflect the recipient/destination derived at the time of locking.
8) Assert business validations:
   - Address ownership enforced: the same member who created the address can lock it successfully.
   - Locking creates an immutable address snapshot reflecting the address content at lock time.
   - Re-locking behavior is consistent (idempotent or cleanly versioned) while preserving correct snapshot data.

Validations:
- Lock-for-checkout results in an immutable snapshot that can be retrieved via the address snapshots endpoints.
- Snapshot shipping details (recipient name/phone and destination fields) match the address values at the moment of lock, not later changes (later changes are not required for this scenario; the snapshot correctness is validated directly).

plan.thinking: IShoppingMallWishlist.ICreate is a create DTO for the wishlist container. It has x-autobe-database-schema = shopping_mall_wishlists, so it is collectable and maps directly to the shopping_mall_wishlists table. The owning foreign key shopping_mall_member_id is not provided in the DTO body; it comes from the authenticated member context, so add that as a collector reference.

Collects IShoppingMallSnapshotParty.ICreate to shopping_mall_snapshot_parties. DTO maps directly to columns party_type, party_id, can_view, while shopping_mall_snapshot_id is derived from the {snapshotId} path parameter in POST /shoppingMall/admin/snapshots/{snapshotId}/parties.

Collects IShoppingMallSnapshotPayload.ICreate to shopping_mall_snapshot_payloads (stores snapshot serialized payload). The only referenced foreign key (shopping_mall_snapshot_id) comes from the endpoint path parameter snapshotId, not from the DTO body.
IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate is a Create DTO with x-autobe-database-schema set to shopping_mall_categories, meaning it is persisted to that table. Collectable.

IShoppingMallSnapshot.ICreate is collectable: it has x-autobe-database-schema='shopping_mall_snapshots' and represents inserting a snapshot metadata record (with snapshot payload/parties handled in related tables). No additional FK references are required from path parameters or auth context beyond what the DTO body already contains.

Collects IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate to shopping_mall_products. The DTO is a create request and directly maps its provided fields (category id, code, name, description, is_featured) into the shopping_mall_products row, while ownership fields like shopping_mall_seller_id are derived server-side from the authenticated seller context.

Collects IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate into shopping_mall_product_images. This is a create DTO that results in an inserted row into the product-images table (href/alt_text/display_order + soft-delete initialized to null). The only foreign key (shopping_mall_product_id) is included in the DTO body, so there are no additional external references from path params or auth context.

Collects inventory movement creation into shopping_mall_inventory_records. The Create DTO includes the required foreign key shopping_mall_product_variant_id and all quantity fields mapped directly to the table columns, so no external references (path/auth) are needed.

Collects IShoppingMallProductVariant.ICreate into shopping_mall_product_variants for insertion. The DTO carries shopping_mall_product_id plus all sell-side fields mapped directly to shopping_mall_product_variants columns; the collector needs no additional FK references from path or auth context beyond the existing ownership validation handled at service layer.
Collects IShoppingMallProductSnapshot.ICreate to shopping_mall_snapshots since the DTO schema specifies x-autobe-database-schema = shopping_mall_snapshots (direct metadata insert).

Collects IShoppingMallProductVariantSnapshot.ICreate into the shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots table. The DTO maps directly to the snapshot row fields (including shopping_mall_product_variant_id) and is used to insert a new record, so a collector is needed.

Collects IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ICreate into shopping_mall_wishlist_items. Body provides shopping_mall_product_id; wishlist id comes from the {wishlistId} path parameter, while DB-managed fields are set by persistence.

Collects IShoppingMallCartItem.ICreate into shopping_mall_cart_items. The table is explicitly mapped via x-autobe-database-schema on the DTO, and the create flow inserts a new cart item row with variant id and quantity (subtotal computed) while scoping to the owning cart via cartId/auth context.

Collectable: IShoppingMallCart.ICreate is used to create a shopping cart container and maps directly to the database table shopping_mall_carts (server initializes fields; member ownership is provided by the authorized actor/session).

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate maps directly to the shopping_mall_orders table (x-autobe-database-schema = shopping_mall_orders). As a Create DTO used as request payload to persist data, it is collectable. It requires an existing payment reference provided in the body, and ownership linkage comes from authorized member context, so there are no extra path-parameter references needed; the databaseSchemaName for this DTO is shopping_mall_orders.

Collects IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate to shopping_mall_order_items (direct mapping via x-autobe-database-schema). All required foreign keys are provided in the DTO body, so no external references from path/auth context are needed.

Collects IShoppingMallPayment.ICreate to shopping_mall_payments. The DTO schema includes x-autobe-database-schema="shopping_mall_payments" and maps user-provided amount/currency/provider/provider_reference; record creation is backed by this table.

IShoppingMallShipmentConfirmation.ICreate is a create payload whose properties map directly to columns in shopping_mall_shipment_confirmations (shopping_mall_shipment_id, confirmation_type, confirmed_at, and optional tracking/note fields). Therefore a collector should be generated for this DTO to persist the record in that table. No additional FK references are missing from the DTO beyond what is included in the request body.

Collects IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ICreate into shopping_mall_cancellation_requests. The DTO has x-autobe-database-schema mapping to the table, and the create payload includes the required foreign key shopping_mall_order_item_id via orderItemId, plus reason; timestamps/status/id are system-populated by the server.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate is a Create payload that persists data into the shopping_mall_refund_requests table (x-autobe-database-schema). Therefore a collector is needed to create this record. The DTO carries orderItemId and customerReason mapped to shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_order_item_id and customer_reason, so there are no missing foreign-key references from path or auth context.

Collects IShoppingMallReview.ICreate to shopping_mall_reviews. The DTO is a create payload with x-autobe-database-schema mapping to the shopping_mall_reviews table; order-item id, rating, body, and is_public are in the request body, while customer id is derived from auth but not represented as a missing FK reference in references[].

Collects address creation requests into shopping_mall_addresses. The DTO fields map directly to shopping_mall_addresses columns, and the owning customer reference (shopping_mall_customer_id) is supplied from the authenticated actor/session context, so a collector is required.

Collectable: IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate inserts a new shipment grouping row into shopping_mall_shipments (it has x-autobe-database-schema = shopping_mall_shipments). Required fields include shopping_mall_order_id and shopping_mall_order_item_ids, which the service uses to derive seller_snapshot_id and bind the shipment to the order and selected items. No additional foreign keys need to be sourced from path params or auth context beyond what is already present in the DTO.

Collectable: IShoppingMallMemberEmailVerification.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_member_email_verifications (x-autobe-database-schema). import { TypedBody, TypedParam, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { IPageIShoppingMallCategory } from "../../../../api/structures/IPageIShoppingMallCategory";
import { IShoppingMallCategory } from "../../../../api/structures/IShoppingMallCategory";
import { AdminAuth } from "../../../../decorators/AdminAuth";
import { AdminPayload } from "../../../../decorators/payload/AdminPayload";
import { deleteShoppingMallAdminCategoriesCategoryId } from "../../../../providers/deleteShoppingMallAdminCategoriesCategoryId";
import { getShoppingMallAdminCategoriesCategoryId } from "../../../../providers/getShoppingMallAdminCategoriesCategoryId";
import { patchShoppingMallAdminCategories } from "../../../../providers/patchShoppingMallAdminCategories";
import { postShoppingMallAdminCategories } from "../../../../providers/postShoppingMallAdminCategories";
import { putShoppingMallAdminCategoriesCategoryId } from "../../../../providers/putShoppingMallAdminCategoriesCategoryId";

@Controller("/shoppingMall/admin/categories")
export class ShoppingmallAdminCategoriesController {
  /**
   * Create a new category in the shopping mall catalog.
   *
   * This operation is the administrative entry point for the platform’s category hierarchy. Categories are used to organize products for storefront browsing, including optional one-level nesting where a category may reference exactly one parent category (child category), while deeper nesting is not allowed.
   *
   * Only administrator actors are permitted to perform this action. Non-administrator attempts to create categories must be rejected.
   *
   * The operation persists the category’s customer-facing name and description, its stable URL identifier (slug), and its browsing configuration (visibility and display_order). When a parent category is provided, it defines the one-level nesting relationship that determines how customers will see the category structure: the parent acts as the primary category, and the newly created category becomes the subcategory under it.
   *
   * Validation and consistency rules include:
   *
   * - The specified slug must be unique.
   * - If parent_category_id is provided, the parent/child relationship must satisfy the one-level nesting rule (no deeper nesting).
   *
   * After successful creation, the system makes the new category available for customer browsing immediately so that subsequent customer category list views reflect the latest category structure and text.
   *
   * Related operations:
   *
   * - Administrators can edit an existing category’s name/description, which updates what customers see in listings.
   * - Administrators can delete a category; deleting a category hides it from browsing and moves affected products to an uncategorized state.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Creation payload for the category, including optional one-level nesting via parent_category_id.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor admin
   * @x-autobe-specification Implementation guidance for POST /categories.
   *
   * 1) Authorization
   * - Require admin actor authorization. Reject non-admin requests.
   *
   * 2) Input validation
   * - Validate name and description are present and meet any schema/business constraints.
   * - Validate slug is provided and normalized as a URL-safe identifier consistent with category routing expectations.
   * - Enforce uniqueness of slug using shopping_mall_categories @@unique([slug]).
   * - Validate display_order is provided and is an integer.
   * - Validate visibility is provided and corresponds to allowed visibility states (enforced by service/domain rules).
   * - If parent_category_id is provided:
   *   - Load the parent category by id from shopping_mall_categories.
   *   - Enforce the one-level nesting constraint: the created category must be at depth 2 at most (i.e., the parent must not itself be a child of another category for deeper nesting). Concretely, ensure parent_category.parent_category_id is null; if it is not null, reject.
   *
   * 3) Database transaction
   * - Start a transaction.
   * - Create a new shopping_mall_categories row with:
   *   - parent_category_id (nullable)
   *   - name, description, slug, visibility, display_order
   * - Set created_at/updated_at via database defaults or service logic as implemented.
   * - Commit the transaction.
   *
   * 4) Response
   * - Return the created category entity representation.
   *
   * 5) Error handling
   * - If slug already exists: return an application-level conflict/validation error.
   * - If parent_category_id does not exist: return not-found/validation error.
   * - If parent violates one-level nesting eligibility: return a validation error.
   *
   * 6) Side effects
   * - No background jobs are required for customer visibility; ensure subsequent reads will include the new category according to visibility.
   *
   * 7) Consistency with schema comments
   * - Ensure deleted_at is not set during creation; a newly created category must be treated as visible based on visibility and not marked deleted.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async create(
    @AdminAuth()
    admin: AdminPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate,
  ): Promise<IShoppingMallCategory> {
    try {
      return await postShoppingMallAdminCategories({
        admin,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of shopping mall categories for browsing purposes.
   *
   * This operation is used by the storefront to present category entries using the latest stored category fields: the human-readable `name` and `description`, together with the one-level parent/child structure supported by categories. The underlying category model allows an optional `parent_category_id` to represent that a category can be nested under exactly one parent, enabling one-level subcategory browsing.
   *
   * The system must ensure customer browsing remains consistent with administrator-managed category lifecycle rules. When an administrator edits the category `name` or `description`, those updated values must be reflected in the browsing results produced by this operation. When an administrator deletes a category, that category must be hidden from customer browsing, and products that were previously linked to the deleted category become uncategorized; therefore this operation must exclude records that are no longer visible.
   *
   * Authorization-wise, this endpoint only returns category data and does not modify any state. Only listing/browsing is performed, so callers must have permission to browse categories under their actor scope.
   *
   * Filtering/pagination expectations: the request body controls pagination and optional ordering/search fields, while the response returns a page of category summaries optimized for list rendering. For nesting, the response should preserve the one-level relationship by including parent/child placement information according to the schema relationship where `parent_category_id` is optional and `childCategories` is derived from it.
   *
   * Related operations: Administrators manage category creation, editing, and deletion through write operations (not covered here). Customers view categories through this listing operation, and then navigate into product browsing pages that use the selected category context.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search and pagination criteria for categories listing.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor admin
   * @x-autobe-specification Query shopping_mall_categories and return a paginated list of category summaries.
   *
   * 1) Parse requestBody criteria for pagination (page size, cursor/offset if supported by IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest) and optional filters (e.g., visibility, parent/slug/name search) as defined by the request DTO.
   * 2) Apply filtering to shopping_mall_categories:
   *    - Only include categories that are visible for browsing according to the `visibility` column.
   *    - Exclude categories with `deleted_at` set (category records treated as hidden).
   * 3) Apply sorting:
   *    - If request specifies an order, map it to allowed columns (e.g., display_order, updated_at, created_at).
   * 4) Build nesting context for one-level hierarchy:
   *    - Include parent category identifier (from `parent_category_id`) in each returned summary so clients can render primary/subcategory placement.
   *    - Do not attempt multi-level nesting beyond the one-level rule.
   * 5) Execute in a single read transaction (no writes).
   * 6) Return IPageIShoppingMallCategory.ISummary containing pagination metadata and the list of category summaries.
   *
   * Edge cases:
   * - If no categories match filters, return an empty page (pagination metadata should still be present).
   * - If parent/child composition is requested, ensure it does not imply deeper-than-one-level nesting.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async index(
    @AdminAuth()
    admin: AdminPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIShoppingMallCategory.ISummary> {
    try {
      return await patchShoppingMallAdminCategories({
        admin,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve a single shopping mall category by its identifier for customer-facing browsing.
   *
   * This operation is intended for storefront and customer UI flows where the user selects a category link and needs the latest category name and description. Categories are created, edited, and removed by administrators only; customers are restricted to viewing category information and browsing products through the category grouping.
   *
   * The operation reads from `shopping_mall_categories`, which stores `name`, `description`, `slug`, `visibility`, and `display_order` along with timestamps. The category may be arranged with an optional one-level nesting relationship via `parent_category_id` to support primary/subcategory browsing.
   *
   * Behavior and visibility rules are aligned with administrative category lifecycle:
   * - If a category has been removed (record has `deleted_at` set), it must not be treated as browseable by customers.
   * - If the category is not meant to be displayed to customers according to its `visibility` value, it must not be returned for customer browsing.
   *
   * Authorization: this endpoint is a read operation for customer browsing. It must allow unauthenticated visitors and authenticated customers to view browseable category details, while write operations remain administrator-only.
   *
   * Related operations: this endpoint is typically used alongside a categories list endpoint (which returns multiple categories with the category/subcategory structure) so that the UI can show a list first and then fetch the detail for a selected category. After an administrator edits the category name/description, subsequent calls to this endpoint must reflect the latest stored values.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param categoryId Target category identifier (UUID) to fetch a single category record.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor admin

  /**
   * Retrieve the authenticated customer’s order history as a paginated list of order summaries.
   *
   * This operation supports browsing by applying pagination and ordering so customers can reliably locate their newest orders first. The list entries include each order’s human reference (order code/number), placed date (order date), computed total price, and the overall order status. The operation is designed specifically for the customer’s “order history” use case described in the requirements: the customer can view a list of their orders in a paginated format sorted by newest first.
   *
   * Only orders that are considered successfully created after checkout/payment succeeded are included. If a customer has no successful orders, the result must be an empty list rather than an error.
   *
   * Data is backed by the order header records in shopping_mall_orders (ownership via shopping_customer_id) and must be filtered by the success state of the related payment attempt in shopping_mall_payments (shopping_payment_id). Order fulfillment-related state shown as the “overall order status” is derived from the associated order items and shipment workflow, using the status fields stored in shopping_mall_order_items (line_item_status) and shipment records in shopping_mall_shipments (status).
   *
   * Security and data isolation: the authenticated actor must be constrained to their own orders via shopping_mall_orders.shopping_customer_id. This endpoint must not expose other customers’ orders.
   *
   * Related operations: customers may also view full order details (a different endpoint) where each order item’s current item status is displayed within the order details view. That detailed view is separate from this history-list operation which returns only the summary fields optimized for list browsing.
   *
   * Expected behavior: when the requested page has no items, return an empty page data set with pagination metadata corresponding to the requested parameters.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Order history browsing criteria including pagination controls (and any supported filters) for the authenticated customer.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor member
   * @x-autobe-specification Implement a customer-scoped order history list operation.
   *
   * 1) Authorization / scope
   * - Require authentication as a member.
   * - Resolve the authenticated member’s id (shopping_mall_members.id).
   * - Only consider shopping_mall_orders where shopping_customer_id == authenticatedMemberId.
   *
   * 2) Input handling (request body)
   * - Parse shopping_mall_orders list request criteria from IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.
   * - Apply pagination (page size / cursor / offset depending on DTO definition) and sorting.
   * - Enforce newest-first ordering by using shopping_mall_orders.placed_at (descending) as the primary sort key.
   *
   * 3) “Successfully created” rule
   * - Join shopping_mall_orders with shopping_mall_payments using shopping_payment_id.
   * - Filter to include only orders whose related payment.status represents success (exact success value must be inferred from implementation/config in Realize Agent; if the DTO/status mapping exists, use it).
   * - Ensure failed payment attempts do not contribute any orders to the list.
   *
   * 4) Overall order status derivation
   * - For each candidate order, derive overall order status based on associated workflow:
   *   - Use shopping_mall_order_items.line_item_status for item-level state.
   *   - Use shopping_mall_shipments.status when shipment grouping affects shipped/delivered/cancelled outcomes.
   * - Return the aggregated/overall status in the order summary according to existing business-rule conventions used by other order endpoints.
   *
   * 5) Total price computation for summary
   * - Compute order total price as the sum of purchased line totals using:
   *   - shopping_mall_order_items.seller_price_at_purchase * shopping_mall_order_items.quantity.
   * - Do not recompute from payments unless required by the existing DTO; prefer item totals for consistency with line-item captures.
   *
   * 6) Pagination query strategy
   * - Use a two-phase approach for large datasets:
   *   a) Query order ids with applied filters and newest-first ordering plus pagination.
   *   b) Load aggregates (overall status, total price, and summary fields) for only those ids.
   *
   * 7) Soft-deletion visibility
   * - Apply shopping_mall_orders.deleted_at: exclude orders where deleted_at is not null from active views.
   *
   * 8) Edge cases
   * - If no successful orders exist for the customer, return an empty data array with pagination metadata.
   * - If a requested page is beyond the last page, return empty data with metadata consistent with the pagination implementation.
   *
   * 9) Response mapping
   * - Map each selected order to IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary fields (order code/number, placed_at as order date, computed total, overall status, and any summary identifiers required by the DTO).
   *
   * 10) Error handling
   * - Return appropriate error responses for unauthenticated access (authorization middleware), malformed request body (validation), and internal failures during aggregation queries.

  @TypedRoute.Patch()

import { TypedBody, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia from "typia";

import { IShoppingMallOrder } from "../../../../../api/structures/IShoppingMallOrder";
import { AdminAuth } from "../../../../../decorators/AdminAuth";
import { AdminPayload } from "../../../../../decorators/payload/AdminPayload";
import { patchShoppingMallAdminOrdersOversight } from "../../../../../providers/patchShoppingMallAdminOrdersOversight";

@Controller("/shoppingMall/admin/orders/oversight")
export class ShoppingmallAdminOrdersOversightController {
  /**
   * Administrators use this endpoint to perform order oversight decisions that force the platform to apply cancellation or refund outcomes to order items and/or entire orders.
   *
   * This operation is designed for the administrative workflows described in the requirements where an administrator must be able to force-cancel an individual order item or all applicable items in an order, and similarly force-refund an individual order item or all relevant items in an order. The business outcomes include updating the affected order item workflow status, driving the corresponding refund behavior, and ensuring inventory quantities are restored for the affected product variants.
   *
   * The request targets existing records in `shopping_mall_orders` (order header), `shopping_mall_order_items` (line items with `line_item_status`), and `shopping_mall_shipments` (seller-specific fulfillment batches per order). Because order oversight is performed at item-level isolation, the implementation must select only the relevant `shopping_mall_order_items` rows for the specified target, and must ensure shipment-related visibility remains consistent after the status transitions.
   *
   * For dispute resolution and audit trails, administrative oversight must preserve snapshot trail integrity. The system must not retroactively alter or remove existing snapshot metadata/content; if the force-cancel/force-refund results require recording an additional final decision transition, new snapshot records must be created without violating the snapshot immutability and single-final-decision principles.
   *
   * Retry safety: if the oversight action is retried, the implementation must avoid creating multiple conflicting snapshots for the same final outcome state and must keep the order-item status transition consistent with already-applied final decisions.
   *
   * Related operations: this endpoint is the write-side command used by administrators for forced cancellation/refund oversight. After performing oversight, administrators may use existing order/shipments/order-item retrieval operations (not defined here) to observe the updated `line_item_status` and shipment states. If there are cancellation/refund request records in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` / `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, the implementation must ensure that the forced outcome remains compatible with their seller-decision workflow and does not create rule-breaking transitions.
   *
   * Error handling: if the targeted order-item or order is not found, is outside the administrator's oversight scope, or if applying a decision would contradict the ordering of terminal states already present in `shopping_mall_order_items.line_item_status`, the operation must reject the request. If some order items in an order are not eligible for customer-driven cancellation/refund, the forced oversight must still apply consistently to the affected items as required, without incorrectly changing unrelated items.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Administrative oversight command payload to force-cancel or force-refund an order item or an entire order, applying the same business outcomes as approved cancellation/refund and ensuring inventory restoration and snapshot trail integrity.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor admin
   * @x-autobe-specification Implementation guidance for Realize Agent.
   *
   * 1) Authorization
   * - Allow only authenticated administrators (admin actor per authorization rules).
   * - Reject non-admin callers.
   *
   * 2) Input parsing and target resolution
   * - Parse request body to determine:
   *   a) scope: single order item vs entire order
   *   b) action: force-cancel vs force-refund
   *   c) target identifiers (orderId and optionally orderItemId) and any optional reason fields.
   * - When the scope is 'order', load `shopping_mall_order_items` by `shopping_mall_order_id`.
   * - When the scope is 'item', load exactly one `shopping_mall_order_items` by `id`, and also verify it belongs to the provided `shopping_mall_orders.id` when both are supplied.
   *
   * 3) Eligibility and state transition rules
   * - For each targeted order item, read current `line_item_status`.
   * - Enforce compatibility with item-level rules: if applying the forced action would contradict the ordering of statuses already present in `line_item_status` (e.g., later terminal states), reject the operation or reject per-item application while preserving consistent outcomes according to business rules.
   * - Apply forced cancellation/refund outcomes consistently even when the customer-driven cancellation eligibility would differ, while still respecting terminal state ordering.
   *
   * 4) Side effects: refund/inventory and statuses
   * - Update targeted `shopping_mall_order_items.line_item_status` to the forced outcome state.
   * - Ensure the forced cancellation/refund outcomes trigger the same business outcomes as the approved seller path: refund customer amount and restore stock quantities for `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`.
   *   - Inventory restoration must be implemented via appending new `shopping_mall_inventory_records` entries (or whatever the system layer uses) so historical integrity remains.
   *
   * 5) Snapshot integrity and retry safety
   * - Do NOT modify or delete existing `shopping_mall_snapshots` and `shopping_mall_snapshot_payloads` rows.
   * - Create new snapshot metadata in `shopping_mall_snapshots` only when required to record a final oversight transition.
   * - Ensure the new snapshot's `source_type`, `source_entity_id`, and relevant linkage fields (`source_order_id` / `source_order_item_id` / `source_seller_id` if applicable) match the decision context.
   * - Create snapshot payload in `shopping_mall_snapshot_payloads` as needed (1:1 by `shopping_mall_snapshot_id`).
   * - Create visibility entries in `shopping_mall_snapshot_parties` only as required so that owners and administrators can view the dispute trail.
   * - Retry safety: before inserting a new final decision snapshot, check whether a snapshot already exists for the target item/order with the same final outcome (based on snapshot source keys and/or reason/created timeline rules) and avoid duplicates.
   *
   * 6) Shipments and order-level recalculation
   * - Because shipments group order items per seller, ensure any shipment status derived fields remain consistent after item status updates.
   * - After item updates, recalculate order-level outcome (if there is such derived status elsewhere in the data model layer) so that overall order status becomes 'cancelled' or 'refunded' when all relevant items are in the corresponding terminal state.
   *
   * 7) Transactions and concurrency
   * - Wrap the oversight application per request in a transaction.
   * - Use row-level locking or optimistic checks to prevent conflicting admin retries or concurrent admin actions from producing inconsistent status transitions.
   *
   * 8) Response mapping
   * - Return a result object containing:
   *   - which target was applied (orderId and/or orderItemId)
   *   - action type
   *   - final statuses applied
   *   - counts of updated items and any items skipped/rejected with reason codes.
   *
   * 9) Error scenarios
   * - 404/NotFound when order or order item does not exist.
   * - 409/Conflict when the current `line_item_status` does not allow the forced transition order.
   * - 422/UnprocessableEntity when request is structurally valid but violates business transition rules.
   *
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async applyOrderOversight(
    @AdminAuth()
    admin: AdminPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate,
  ): Promise<void> {
    try {
      return await patchShoppingMallAdminOrdersOversight({
        admin,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
